definition: Timbre is a property of a sound that listeners perceive as different from pitch, though the two can influence each other in perception and may sometimes be confused. In this context, timbre refers to the aspect of a tone that can vary, for example, in ways described as darker or lighter.

reasons: The packet supports pitch–timbre interference/confusion and a ‘dark’ timbre example, but it does not support the added ‘lighter’ descriptor or present timbre as a general property contrasted with pitch in definitional form.
The packet does not provide an explicit definition of “timbre” as a sound property perceived as different from pitch.

The packet mentions “pitch-timbre confusions” and examples involving “dark” timbre and pitch labeling, but it does not state that timbre is “different from pitch” or describe the general listener-perception distinction described in the definition.

The definition’s claim that “timbre refers to the aspect of a tone that can vary” (e.g., “darker or lighter”) is only partially supported by the packet’s example of “dark” timbre; the packet does not clearly support the broader phrasing.
